note: Short excerpts for the data-collection and wind-channel reads. Each quote is the sentence the screen applies. The rest of the instrument is not copied here. A superseded note stays, and it is not the live duty.

entries.heading: Cumulative Impacts
entries.quote: Some EIA reports have failed to fully account for the interface with other development projects in the vicinity and, hence, failed to address the cumulative impacts of the projects involved. These development projects should be identified during data collection stage and the extent of the cumulative impacts assessed.

entries.instrument: Technical Memorandum on the Environmental Impact Assessment Process
entries.heading: Cumulative environmental effects
entries.quote: there may be interactions between the environmental impacts of the project and the environmental impacts of other developments, resulting in accumulation of impacts and affecting the cumulative environmental impacts.

entries.instrument: Technical Memorandum on the Environmental Impact Assessment Process
entries.heading: Evaluation of the Residual Environmental Impacts
entries.quote: The residual environmental impacts refer to the net environmental impacts after mitigation, taking into account the background environmental conditions and the impacts from existing, committed and planned projects.

entries.instrument: Technical Circular No. 1/06 — Air Ventilation Assessment
entries.heading: No absolute benchmark
entries.quote: The framework developed at this stage does not provide an absolute benchmark standard against which the air ventilation impacts can be confirmed to be acceptable or unacceptable. The framework would however, enable comparison of design options in external air ventilation terms and identification of potential problem areas for design improvements.

entries.heading: Wind velocity ratio
entries.quote: Wind VR is defined as Vp/V∞ (V pedestrian/V infinity). V∞ captures the wind velocity at the top of the wind boundary layer (typically assumed to be around 400 m to 600 m above city centre, or at a height wind is unaffected by the urban roughness below). V∞ is taken as the wind availability of the site. Vp captures the wind velocity at the pedestrian level (2 m above ground) after taking into account the effects of buildings and urban features.

entries.heading: Site and local spatial average velocity ratio
entries.quote: Comparing performances of design options using the spatial average VR (both SVR and LVR) is recommended.
